source: National Survey of Family Growth (NCHS) public-use respondent files, pooled: 1995 (Cycle 5), 2002, 2006-2010, 2011-2013, 2013-2015, 2015-2017, 2017-2019 and 2022-2023 female files; male files 2002 onward. Respondents aged 15-44 (15-49 from 2015); first marriages begun 1964-2023
target: Annual rate of first-marriage dissolution (divorce, annulment or separation) per marriage-year from the wedding day; widowhood censored (Poisson rate, not a probability)
population: U.S. household population; the women's models use women's FIRST marriages (husbands of any marital history), the wife's own report; models_both_sexes add men's first marriages with respondent-level inputs only
weights: NSFG final weights rescaled within each file to average 1 over all its respondents (so each cycle counts in proportion to its sample size), then normalised to mean 1 over the marriages, times exposure

inputs.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = first year)
inputs.wife_age_at_marriage: wife's age in years on the wedding day
inputs.husband_age_at_marriage: husband's age in years on the wedding day (wife's report)
inputs.wedding_year: calendar year of the wedding; outside the support is extrapolation, so hold it at the support edge and say so
inputs.wife_premarital_sex_years: years between the wife's first sexual intercourse and the wedding (0 if none before the wedding)
inputs.husband_prior_children: Yes/No: husband had children from a prior relationship
inputs.wife_race_ethnicity: Hispanic, White, Black, Other (non-Hispanic unless Hispanic)
inputs.same_race_ethnicity: Same/Different: husband's broad race-ethnicity group versus the wife's
inputs.wife_intact_family: Yes/No: wife lived with both (biological or adoptive) parents from birth to 18
inputs.wife_premarital_birth: Yes/No: the wife had a birth before the wedding
inputs.wife_premarital_partners: wife's number of male sex partners before the first marriage: 0, 1, 2, 3-4, 5-9, 10+
inputs.wife_ba_by_wedding: Yes/No: the wife had a bachelor's degree by the wedding (from degree dates)
inputs.wife_mother_education: wife's mother's education: <HS, HS, Some college, BA+, No mother figure
inputs.wife_mother_age_first_birth: wife's mother's age at her first birth: <18, 18-19, 20-24, 25+, No mother figure
inputs.wife_religion_raised: religion the wife was raised in: None, Catholic, Protestant, Other

abstain: wife previously married (only first marriages of women are in the data)
any partner outside the age-at-marriage support
wedding year after the support (hold at the edge, label it)

extra_models.label: Poisson tree, depth 4
extra_models.note: evaluated and exported for inspection; weaker than the others held out, so not a scoring model

shipped_model: mean survival of additive_spline and gradient_boosting

comparison_vs_2002_lens.note: Same person folds. lens2002_2002data refits the published 2002 lens (same inputs, same spline GLM) on the 2002-cycle training women only, with wedding_year held inside 1972-2002 as the app does; additive_2002features_pooled uses the same inputs on all cycles; additive_spline adds the new inputs.

inputs_both_sexes.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = first year)
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_age_at_marriage: the reporting spouse's age on the wedding day
inputs_both_sexes.wedding_year: calendar year of the wedding; outside the support is extrapolation, so hold it at the support edge and say so
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_premarital_sex_years: years between the reporting spouse's first intercourse and the wedding (0 if none before)
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_sex: Female/Male: which spouse reported (the data are not couples)
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_premarital_birth: Yes/No: the reporting spouse had (or fathered) a birth before the wedding
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_race_ethnicity: Hispanic, White, Black, Other (non-Hispanic unless Hispanic)
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_intact_family: Yes/No: lived with both parents from birth to 18
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_ba_by_wedding: Yes/No: bachelor's degree by the wedding
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_mother_education: wife's mother's education: <HS, HS, Some college, BA+, No mother figure
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_mother_age_first_birth: wife's mother's age at her first birth: <18, 18-19, 20-24, 25+, No mother figure
inputs_both_sexes.respondent_religion_raised: religion the wife was raised in: None, Catholic, Protestant, Other

population_reference.about: Survey-weighted quantiles of held-out predicted first-marriage dissolution (divorce, annulment or separation) within each horizon of the wedding, for the 29,202 women's first marriages in NSFG 1995-2023, each scored by models fitted on the other four person folds with her own inputs and real wedding year; the lens number is 1 minus the mean survival of additive_spline and gradient_boosting, as the app computes it. Each pK is a list aligned to horizons. Subgroup cells have at least 100 unweighted marriages; Unknown and Not asked levels are omitted. Built by reproducibility/nsfg_pooled_first_marriage/train_pooled.py.

wife_ba_by_wedding.label: Wife had a bachelor's degree by the wedding

wife_intact_family.label: Wife lived with both parents to 18

wife_religion_raised.label: Religion the wife was raised in

wife_premarital_birth.label: Wife had a birth before the wedding

population_reference_both_sexes.about: As population_reference, for the both-sexes models (models_both_sexes) over 43,336 first marriages reported by women (1995-2023) and men (2002-2023); subgroup respondent_sex splits by who reported.

respondent_age_band.label: Reporting spouse's age at the wedding

partner_distribution.about: Weighted joint frequencies of partner traits given the respondent's own coarse traits, in women's first marriages pooled over NSFG 1995-2023 (the wife's report). Conditioning cells have at least 30 unweighted marriages; a partner profile is listed only when at least 10 marriages in the cell share it, and shares are renormalised over the listed profiles (coverage = weighted share they cover). Marriages whose cycle did not ask a trait (husband's prior children in 1995, husband's race in 2022-2023) are left out of that table. gap_bin is husband minus wife age at the wedding (2022-2023 husband ages are 5-year band mid-points); gap_values gives the weighted median gap in each bin, the value the app scores.

ood.method: squared Mahalanobis distance on the model inputs; percentile against held-out people (5 person folds)

models_extended.label: Additive spline Poisson GLM (women), current inputs + all new blocks

heldout.evaluation: train_pooled.py person folds (5); weighted Poisson deviance vs the training-fold constant; paired person bootstrap (1000)

categories: Parents split up or a parent died

feature_names: cat__wife_family_origin_Parents split up or a parent died

models_extended_note: Held-out comparison of richer childhood inputs (2026-10-20, extended_predictors.py). Not scored by the app until the form asks for them. Blocks whose held-out difference had a 95% CI above zero: none.

inputs_extended.wife_family_origin: who the wife grew up with: Both parents (both to 18, INTACT18) / Stepfamily (a step-father or another mother figure at 14) / Never-married single parent (biological parents not married when she was born, PARMARR) / Parents split up or a parent died (married at her birth but not intact; the public files do not separate divorce from death) / Other / Not asked (1995, 2002, 2022-2023)
inputs_extended.wife_attend14: how often she attended religious services at 14 (ATTND14), seven answers from Never to More than once a week; Not asked in 1995, 2002 and 2022-2023
inputs_extended.wife_religion_raised_detail: religion she was raised in (RELRAISD), eight answers; Not asked where the cycle lacks it
